order.why: Rule 1 on a textbook stopping muon: 108 cm flat at ~50k then a monotone Bragg rise to 260k at 5001 (with a Michel-like blob 20003 4 cm off that end), so the cool start 5000 is the vertex.

Deg-4 junction where p4 shows seg 8001 as a textbook monotone stopping-proton profile falling from 247k at 8000 back to MIP at 8002, the 34.5 cm shower runs away to 8001, and three satellite blob pairs sit within 15 cm.

Rule 1 perfect: both prongs rise away from 12003 - 64 cm pion stopping at 90k at 12002 and 11.8 cm proton with a textbook monotone Bragg to 190k at 12001, opening 122 degrees so not the collinear trap.

Rule 1 plus rule 3: the 250 cm muon path cools monotonically from its textbook Bragg stop at 14003 all the way back through 14007 to 14005, where two short heavily-ionising prongs sit (4.7 cm at 125k, 5.9 cm rising to 230k); 14005 is also the most upstream point at z=68.
Rule 1: deg-3 junction with two protons and a muon rising away, and the 30cm muon of the neighbouring cluster starts 1.9cm from it.

Rule 1 at a 72 deg junction: the 11.6 cm heavy prong spikes to 360k at its far end 8000 (stopping proton) while the 19.4 cm MIP prong leaves the other way, and both prongs carry a charge blob in their first bin at 8002.

Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away at a clear 126 deg V: the 77cm muon Braggs to 210k at 16000 and the 21.6cm pion Braggs to 180k at 16003, where a 4.9cm proton starts and Braggs to 265k, so 16003 is a pion secondary and 16002 is the vertex.
The event contains a single 0.3 cm cluster and exactly one candidate vertex, so the answer is forced; there is nothing else in the detector to choose between.
Rule 1: degree-3 junction where all three prongs (111 cm muon, 13 cm proton to 174k, 18 cm pi+) get hotter going away from it.
Deg-3 junction where the 18 cm proton rises away x1.34 to 132k at 13004 and the 204 cm pion rises away x1.97 to its stop at 13000.

Rule 1: deg-3 where the 5.8 cm proton falls monotonically from 350k at its far end 1000 back to MIP at 1003 (born at 1003), joined by a second 3.5 cm 124k proton stub; the 91 cm prong is flat MIP and exits the top wall.
Rule 1 fully satisfied at a deg-3 vertex: a 199 cm muon Bragging to 115k at 15000, a 5.7 cm 200k proton and a 2.0 cm 169k pi+ all leaving 15002.

p4 shows the 158 cm muon falling from 148k right at the 14000 end along the stopping template, so that end is the stop; 14001 is the MIP start and sits amid a hadronic spray including a 285k e/cm proton blob 31 cm off.

Rule 1: degree-4 junction from which a 363 cm muon rises x3.3 to its Bragg stop at 12000 and a 31 cm proton chain rises monotonically 89k->152k to its stop at 12004, with two sub-cm stubs at the point.

Rule 1 textbook: deg-3 junction with two 8-9 cm protons whose profiles rise monotonically away to 290k and 310k Bragg peaks at 3001 and 3003, plus an 82 cm muon leaving forward, so every prong points away from 3002.
Rule 1: the 16.1 cm proton rises monotonically from 55k at 3002 to 290k at 3001 on the template, the 132 cm muon leaves at 123 deg (not back-to-back), and small EM fragments sit within 2 cm of 3002.

Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away at 140 deg, and the zoom shows a sharp dQ/dx step across 7004 (100k proton side, 50k MIP side); the 45cm muon Braggs to 135k at 7005 where a 13cm decay prong hangs, so rule 3 makes 7005 the far end.
Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away: 48 cm proton x2.23 to 189k at 13004 and 172 cm muon x1.62 forward; the muon later stops with a Michel-like stub at 13007.
Rule 1: degree-3 vertex where the 5.9 cm proton rises 165k to 204k away toward 9006, the 165 cm muon Braggs away at 9000, and an EM bush hangs off the third prong.

The only real object is a 424cm flat-MIP vertical track running wall to wall in y with no Bragg at either end (a cosmic); every other cluster is a sub-6cm isolated blip scattered over 150cm with nothing converging, so any click would be a guess.
Rule 1 plus the hot-blob trap: the 7 cm proton Braggs away to 18002 while the 102 cm muon is flat MIP for 100 cm with only a two-point spike at 18001, i.e. vertex charge and not a Bragg rise.
Rule 8 abstention: four isolated blobs of 3.5 cm or less, spread 30-70 cm apart with no readable direction and no ionizing structure, so any click is as good as another.

Heuristic 8: every cluster is a sub-1cm isolated blip and the ten of them are scattered over the whole detector (z 42 to 411, x -145 to +118) with no track, no dQ/dx gradient and nothing converging anywhere.

Abstaining under heuristic 8 - every one of the 13 clusters is sub-centimetre, giving 14 isolated dots scattered over a 40x60x70 cm region with no fitted track, no dQ/dx gradient and no direction to read.
Textbook three-prong vertex with 56/71/97 deg openings, all prongs forward in z: a 20.1 cm proton rising x1.53 to 181k at 12005, a 10.7 cm proton, and a 24.7 cm MIP muon, all radiating from 12004.
Heuristic 8: all four candidates are isolated single sub-cm dots spread 200-300 cm apart with no fitted segment and no readable direction anywhere in the event, so any click is as good as any other.
Rule 8: 14 clusters all under 2.2cm, no readable direction and no coherent shower apex, so any click is as good as any other - abstaining.

Rule 1: deg-3 with the 13.4 cm proton rising away to 213k, the 6.8 cm pi+ also hotter at its far end and the 281 cm muon leaving; the other deg-3 candidate 12004 is a 166 deg scatter kink inside one long track, i.e. the trap, and is discarded.
Rule 8: the event is four isolated sub-cm dots at z=443-489 with no segment, no direction and no topology of any kind, so any click is as good as any other and I abstain rather than invent a reason.
Rule 8: the whole event is four isolated sub-cm blobs with no segment, no direction and no readable topology, so any click is as good as another.

The 123 cm track shows a monotone 6 cm Bragg decline read into 18000 (it stops there) and only a single-bin blob at 18002, so rule 1 puts the vertex at the cool upstream end 18002, which is also the lower-z end.
Rule 8 case: the whole event is six isolated sub-5 cm dots spread over 200 cm of z with no junction, no Bragg and no readable direction, so any click would be invented rather than reasoned.
Rule 8: the entire event is two isolated sub-cm dots 66 cm apart with no dQ/dx measured on either, so there is no evidence to separate them; abstaining, same policy as evt179303.
Rule 1 in its purest form: a three-prong star where all three segments rise away, two protons ending at 190k and 204k Bragg peaks plus a 122 cm muon, and it is the lowest-z candidate.
Rule 8: six isolated sub-cm dots near z=480-494 and nothing else in the event, no segments and no readable direction, so I abstain rather than pick one blob over another.
Rule 8 abstention: the entire event is three sub-cm dots strung along the x- face with no segments, no dQ/dx gradient and no readable direction.
The only track is a 7.4 cm proton whose profile falls monotonically 235k -> 113k along the proton template from the 4000 end, so 4000 is the Bragg stop and the particle starts at 4001.
Rule 8 abstain: the whole event is six isolated sub-centimetre dots with no track and no readable direction anywhere, so any click would be as good as any other.
Rule 8: all 14 clusters are sub-cm specks with no dQ/dx measured anywhere and no readable direction, so any click is as good as another; abstaining rather than inventing a reason.

Rule 1 at a 121 deg kink: the 13.6 cm proton is sub-MIP (35000) at 10025 and rises to 290000 at 10000 following the proton template, and the 64 cm muon is flat MIP where it meets the vertex before exiting the top wall.

Rule 8 - the whole event is sub-cm fragments (largest cluster 2.4 cm) scattered over ~30 cm with no readable direction, no measurable dQ/dx gradient anywhere, so any click is as good as any other and I abstain rather than invent a reason.

Abstain: the only structure is a muon entering the y=+200 top face, Bragg-rising to a stop at 7000 with a 21 cm Michel hanging off that same end (rule 3 forbids it), and the remaining candidates are two sub-cm blobs on the Michel.

Strongly asymmetric ends on the 344cm muon: a 200k Bragg falling along the template over 10cm at 13000 (5cm mean 124k) versus only a 4cm 130k uptick at 13001 (5cm mean 59k), so it stops at 13000 and starts at 13001, which additionally carries two short stubs of vertex activity.
